title: Understanding MSE Minimization
text: To minimize the Mean Squared Error (MSE) using a constant model, you need to find a value for $$\theta_0$$ that minimizes the sum of squared differences between the predicted and actual values.

title: Using Derivatives
text: Consider using calculus to find the minimum of a function. What does taking the derivative of the MSE with respect to $$\theta_0$$ and setting it to zero tell you?

title: Derivative of MSE
text: The MSE is given by sum{i extbackslash=1}{n}{(y_i-theta_0)**2}. Find the derivative of this expression with respect to $$\theta_0$$.

title: Setting the Derivative to Zero
text: Set the derivative you found to zero and solve for $$\theta_0$$.

title: Interpreting the Result
text: The solution theta_0=sum{i extbackslash=1}{n}{y_i}/n represents the mean of the target values. Why does this make sense for minimizing MSE?
